research_updates.title: Regional impact totals cannot be allocated to 5150 Rogers Road
research_updates.notes: Microsoft's 2026 fact sheet aggregates Bexar and Medina County datacenter construction, operations, taxes, and community programs and says it includes estimated information and projections. The account does not insert those regional totals as project observations or inputs because the publication supplies no building, campus, county, phase, or evidence-state allocation.

source.title: Microsoft's datacenter economic impact in San Antonio, TX
source.notes: The operator fact sheet combines datacenter construction and operations across Bexar and Medina Counties and explicitly includes estimates and projections. Its $2.34 billion construction activity, 17,400 jobs supported, $1.05 billion labor income, 635 direct jobs, additional supported jobs, $48.4 million incremental tax revenue, and $3.3 million community investment figures are not allocated to 5150 Rogers Road and therefore are retained only as research context.

research_updates.title: San Antonio alternative-water share lacks a facility denominator
research_updates.notes: Microsoft reports that 79% of water used at its San Antonio location is recycled, reused, or non-potable. The statement is useful source and cooling context but is not converted into a 5150 Rogers Road quantity because no facility denominator, measurement year, withdrawal/consumption split, or multi-campus allocation is disclosed.

source.title: Inside Microsoft's two-decade push to cut water intensity while scaling for growth
source.notes: Microsoft reports that 79% of water used at its San Antonio location is recycled, reused, or non-potable. The percentage is location-wide and does not disclose a volume, year-specific facility denominator, withdrawal, consumption, or 5150 Rogers Road allocation.

research_updates.title: Search audit — identity, land, physical scale, and appraisal
research_updates.notes: Portal/source family: Bexar Appraisal District property and deed records. Query/identifier: exact address '5150 Rogers' for tax years 2022-2026; inspected property IDs 1094298, 1107340, and 1172617 and deed 20070085721. Date range: 2007 deed and 2022-2026 roll histories. Documents inspected: result table, account detail, improvements, land, roll value, and deed panels. Result: useful — exact Microsoft ownership/address, 36.235 acres, 463,350 square feet, and three account-separated 2025 appraisals; negative for purchase price, investment flow, equipment detail, or building allocation.

source.title: Bexar Appraisal District property search — 5150 Rogers Road Microsoft accounts
source.notes: Exact-address search returned Microsoft real-property account 1094298, equipment/personal-property account 1107340, and solar/wind-equipment account 1172617. The 2025 roll histories report $112,000,000, $91,391,490, and $86,400 of appraised value respectively. Real-property detail reports 36.235 acres and 463,350 square feet of commercial living area; accounts remain separate and assessments are stocks, not investment or receipts.

research_updates.title: Search audit — construction, contractors, and local suppliers
research_updates.notes: Portal/source family: City Development Services granted-permit archive and City procurement search. Query/identifier: exact address '5150 ROGERS RD', Microsoft, permit A2359822, and weekly PDFs for 2008-2026; inspected 2010-12-18, 2011-12-24, 2012-10-06, 2018-05-05, 2018-05-12, 2018-09-08, and 2018-09-15 reports. Date range: 2008-2026. Documents inspected: granted-permit tables and City procurement search results. Result: useful — $2,771,000 renovation permit and named contractors Rogers & O'Brien, Brandt, McKinstry, and Simplex Grinnell; negative for invoices, verified spend, payroll, worker count/residence, contract value, local-retained purchasing, or non-overlap among permits.

source.title: City of San Antonio weekly granted commercial permits, May 12, 2018
source.publisher: City of San Antonio Development Services Department
source.notes: The granted-permit report lists application A2359822 at 5150 Rogers Road for renovations to an existing data center, names Rogers & O'Brien Construction, and reports a $2,771,000 project value. The administrative amount is not verified expenditure, payroll, or local purchasing.

research_updates.title: Search audit — jobs, compliance, incentives, and public cost
research_updates.notes: Portal/source family: City Council ordinances/agreements, Legistar, and active-incentive monitoring. Query/identifier: Microsoft, 5150 Rogers, ordinances 2007-01-18-0073/0074 and 2013-11-21-0817. Date range: 2007-2024 monitoring period. Documents inspected: 2007 ordinance/agreement, 2013 agenda record, and active-agreement row. Result: useful — commitments, reported >$840 million cumulative investment, >75-job floor, investment compliance, and $16,169,082.93 cumulative city taxes abated; negative for actual job count, payroll, annual abatement schedule, CPS CIED disbursement, marginal services, or same-scope net fiscal result. SN4 figures remain separate.

source.title: City of San Antonio active economic incentive agreements
source.notes: The self-reported monitoring table lists the exact 5150 Rogers agreement, $16,169,082.93 in total city taxes abated, investment compliance, and no published actual-job count. research_updates.title: Search audit — property tax bills, payments, and recipients
research_updates.notes: Portal/source family: Bexar County Tax Assessor-Collector account and payment histories. Query/identifier: CAD property IDs 1094298, 1107340, and 1172617; resolved tax accounts 176420480010 and 000001107340. Date range: payment histories from roll year 2008 through 2025, with 2025 selected for normalization. Documents inspected: account balance, levy, jurisdiction, and payment-history panels. Result: useful — both 2025 taxable-account levies were paid in two installments; negative for a payment on the exempt solar/wind account, recipient-level distributions, public-service costs, or a net fiscal total. Refund and transfer rows in earlier years were not netted without a reconciliation.

source.title: Bexar County Tax Assessor-Collector account and payment histories — 5150 Rogers Road
source.notes: CAD-ID searches for 1094298 and 1107340 resolve to tax accounts 176420480010 and 000001107340 at 5150 Rogers Road. research_updates.title: Search audit — electricity, backup generation, and emissions

research_updates.title: Search audit — water, cooling, and wastewater

source.title: San Antonio Water System recycled-water program

research_updates.title: Search audit — operator filings, procurement, and state incentives
research_updates.notes: Portal/source family: Microsoft SEC filings, operator local publications, and Texas Comptroller qualified-data-center registry. source.title: Microsoft Corporation Form 10-K for fiscal year ended June 30, 2026
source.notes: The filing discusses datacenter capital, supply constraints, vendor management, and global operations but does not report San Antonio- or 5150 Rogers-level construction spend, payroll, employees, supplier purchases, electricity, water, emissions, tax, or community transfers.

research_updates.notes: Portal/source family: Microsoft Local, Alamo Colleges recipient pages, Bexar/Texas court search, MSRB/City bond search, and BEA/BLS county data. economic_scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. Peak workforce is distinct from annual employment; source-year labels do not establish fiscal-year boundaries. Original forecasts remain forecasts until realization is verified. No cross-record benefit total is defined. Cumulative project costs are not annual expenditure. Tax receipts and incentive payments remain separate, with inferred taxpayer links disclosed. Contextual research updates do not count as economic amounts. Account tax bills are distinct from cash receipts and incentive-program fees. Tax years, calendar years and fiscal years retain their source basis; separate taxpayer accounts are not consolidated. Municipal developer rebates and taxpayer valuations have distinct subjects. Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. Cumulative community funding remains separate from tax receipts, payroll and modeled multiplier effects. Reported facility power capacity is not measured electricity consumption or peak demand. Permit-listed emergency generators are not runtime, fuel-use or actual-emissions observations. A city largest-taxpayer table's personal-property assessment remains separate from the leasehold real-property account, tax bills, receipts and capital expenditure. TIF loan principal is financing rather than a grant or general-fund receipt; project-generated tax revenue pledged to repayment is retained as a separate public-financing flow and is not added to gross parcel distributions. Water-withdrawal and consumptive permit capacities are regulatory limits rather than measured use. Development-agreement local-labor preferences are requirements rather than realized participation, and operating employee snapshots remain distinct from customers' on-site staff and jobs forecasts. Audited City bond statements distinguish issuance draws, year-end principal, annual principal retired, interest and fees, pledged TIF revenue, debt-service-fund transfers and future principal-plus-interest commitments. These measures are not summed into a benefit or subsidy total. City pledged revenue, City debt-service-fund transfers and the private fund's project TIF revenue applied to loan repayment retain their separate source definitions because only the 2022 transfer and private-fund amount agree exactly. Developer testimony in public meeting minutes is retained as a source-attributed cumulative lower bound; local-contractor spending is not converted into payroll, worker counts, household spending or multiplier effects. Economic-improvement-district cost estimates and maximum owner assessments remain source projections until bond issuance, an assessment schedule, collections and expenditures are verified. A statutory financing cap is not a tax receipt, public expenditure or subsidy. Audited private equipment-financing balances are debt stocks rather than construction spending, public support or community benefit. Reported floor area and occupied-share values describe operating scale and utilization, not employment, revenue, power use or economic output. Contractor and engineer case studies document supplier roles and completion timing but do not establish payment amounts, worker residence, payroll or multiplier effects. State incentive contract amounts, expected jobs and paid-or-certified-to-date fields remain distinct; a zero paid/certified balance at an earlier reporting cutoff does not imply no later claims. Public charging-infrastructure awards are commitments rather than verified disbursements, private project investment or operating benefits. Qualitative payment descriptions without a defensible numeric bound remain research context rather than quantitative records. Program-reported actual qualified investment, certified tax-exemption value and certified tax-credit value remain separate cumulative measures; none is converted into annual spending, a cash grant, local revenue or causal impact. County Business Patterns observations are county-industry context, not project contributions: establishment counts are employer locations rather than data-center facilities, March employment is not an annual average, annual payroll spans the full NAICS cell, and disclosure noise, classification changes and geographic assignment limit comparisons. No CBP change is attributed to a study project. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00052227492: Deep public-evidence audit for Flexential's Minneapolis-Chaska data center on parcel 30.0590020 at 3500 Lyman Boulevard. The review covered Carver County parcel, tax and property-record access points; City of Chaska permit, inspection, agenda, archive, budget, utility and annual-financial-report sources; Minnesota DEED, Revenue, statutory, environmental and utility-regulatory sources; federal workplace-safety search access; current and archived operator, predecessor, career and ESG materials; contractor and supplier references; and education, workforce and recipient-reported community sources for 2013-2026. Eighteen quantitative observations are preserved: a source-projected original investment lower bound; three later non-cumulative permit values; current floor area and critical-load UPS capacity; three annual parcel-tax payments; one current parcel-tax bill; and eight historical Via West Inc. estimated-actual-value observations. Stream's facilities at 1706 and 1708 West Creek Lane, the IP Stream Minneapolis LLC development agreement and its municipal rebates are outside the selected 3500 Lyman Boulevard project boundary and are not duplicated in this fragment; the six base Stream rebate rows require reassignment or removal from this target by the orchestrator because project fragments are append-only. Permit values are administrative estimates and are not summed because scopes may overlap. The current parcel-tax series includes all taxing jurisdictions and special assessments, not City-only receipts or net benefit, and the older citywide taxpayer series is not stitched to current parcel or Flexential values without a direct crosswalk. No synthesis fragment is added because direct observations and even a usable project projection were not found for construction labor, realized operating employment or payroll, supplier payments, metered energy or water, emissions, facility-specific incentive value, public-service costs, community transfers, or a causal county effect. prj_study_im3_building_00172739953: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Switch Las Vegas NAP7, the individual real-property parcel and original SUPERNAP building at 7135 South Decatur Boulevard. The review covered Clark County assessor, Treasurer, Accela permit, planning, air-quality, budget and financial-report access points; Nevada GOED, Department of Taxation and utility-regulatory sources; Switch operator, SEC, career and ESG materials; supplier and contractor references; and recipient-reported community records for 2005-2026. Six direct observations are added without allocating wider Core Campus capital expenditure, combined incentive audits, later facilities or expansions, personal property, tenant equipment, vendor equipment, or company-wide employment to NAP7. The Treasurer record corrects the earlier research note that payment records were uncollected, but the current payment is only a partial fiscal-year amount. No synthesis fragment is added: NAP4 was already operating while NAP7 was under construction in 2008, and the available county panel cannot isolate a NAP7 treatment from earlier facilities, later Core Campus growth, or major non-data-center shocks. modeled_scope_note: Modeled contribution accounts for Apple Mesa / Maricopa County, Switch Citadel / Storey County, and Digital Crossroad Hammond / Lake County. Every required account category and county-comparison module contains sourced evidence or a visibly labeled modeled value. Public support is not netted against unmatched local revenues, unavailable public-service cost is represented by a break-even threshold rather than an invented net margin, county comparisons are descriptive rather than causal, and low-confidence transferred benchmarks remain explicit. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Corrective residual modeled account for Microsoft San Antonio. Eight transferred construction, labor, procurement, operating, and household-output scenarios were removed because their arbitrary capital shares, forecast-realization cases, local-purchase assumptions, and Virginia coefficients were not bounded by project observations. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparisons remain: each uses the project's documented operating-by 2013 anchor and official Bexar County outcome data, has a finite fit-sensitivity envelope, and explicitly makes no causal attribution. The account intentionally remains incomplete because no defensible direct observation or residual model closes the supplier category. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: Corrective DET01 synthesis. Only exact same-period tax-account arithmetic, its explicitly conditional public-cost break-even identity and a unit conversion of displayed municipal meter history remain. Construction, employment, supplier, household, electricity, cooling, emissions, wastewater and county-effect models were removed because the audit did not bound the missing project inputs. This account is intentionally incomplete where direct evidence remains unbounded. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Corrective audit retains six bounded residual calculations only: FY2025 county tax retained after the provisionally linked incentive, the identical marginal-service-cost break-even threshold, conversion of Meta-reported 2024 water withdrawal with source rounding, and three noncausal county comparison gaps with fit sensitivity. Ten models based on arbitrary capital timing, cost shares, FTE ratios, transferred operating/construction multipliers, fleet PUE, or wastewater ratios are removed. Supplier/local-procurement evidence remains unavailable, so the project is intentionally incomplete rather than backfilled. prj_study_im3_building_00464097467: Second-pass modeled contribution account after an expanded public-evidence audit. Direct county permits now cover historical construction values, assessor rolls cover a main-campus parcel stock, a county action covers water-right capacity, Apple reports 2025 campus electricity use, and recipient reports bound two community gifts. Those observations supersede the need for a modeled community proxy but do not supply Apple contractor job-years, construction payroll, annual operating payroll, supplier payments, taxes received, or public-service cost. The construction base therefore retains only the packet's explicit $163 million construction forecast and excludes equipment and historical capital; wide 0.5-1.5 transfer sensitivities expose the mismatch in the last-resort direct construction coefficients. The unsupported local-purchase-share and Virginia induced-output models are removed. No net-fiscal value or public-service-cost break-even is published. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity intervals and no causal-design metadata. prj_study_im3_building_00664938835: Second-pass Expedient Milwaukee / Franklin syntheses retained only after a documented 2007-2026 public-source audit. The account keeps a clearly labeled 2022 ownership-transfer anchor, a PB25-0303-only construction allocation sensitivity, an exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold, a capacity-based electricity engineering sensitivity, and three descriptive county comparison gaps. It removes transferred construction job-years, assumed local-purchase shares, supplier and household output extrapolations, and a duplicate modeled tax row because public sources did not establish realized site employment, supplier geography, household capture, or a need to restate the direct tax observations. PM25-0174 remains excluded for possible overlap. No synthesis is an observed result or fiscal net. prj_study_im3_building_00844389014: Second-pass model review retains one bounded resource identity only. It reproduces Google-reported 2024 Montgomery County water consumption as withdrawal minus discharge after converting displayed million-gallon values to gallons, with a rounding envelope. Direct searches of Clarksville utility/public-works pages, county stormwater records, TDEC/EPA portals and CDE/TVA materials did not surface a building meter, utility bill or a compatible canonical observed-water metric. The amount remains unallocated across the location and inventory buildings; discharge may be engineering-estimated. No transferred multiplier, supplier-retention assumption, energy proxy, fiscal result, public-cost threshold, payroll estimate or causal county outcome is modeled. prj_study_im3_building_00888253616: Residual synthesis after the SV1 public-source audit. It retains one exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold and three reproducible but low-confidence county comparison gaps. The county gaps use 2013-2020 pre-opening histories and an inverse-distance-weighted 20-county benchmark; very wide fit envelopes are retained because Santa Clara County matches poorly. No model converts capacity to consumption, permit value to jobs, or unidentified vendor and community activity to local benefits. prj_study_im3_building_01073720208: Second-pass governed synthesis for Google Council Bluffs. Construction job-years use only two directly observed September 2025 city permit valuations and transfer the published Prince William County prototype coefficients as benchmark equivalents; the four channels are separated and protected by one aggregation. No Pottawattamie County supplier-retention share is imposed because the public audit found contractor names but no payment or vendor-residence ledger. The water row is the unallocated Google Council Bluffs location identity reported for 2024, not a building allocation. No local abatement, exemption realization, franchise-fee amount, electric load, public-service cost, break-even threshold, or net fiscal result is modeled. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity ranges and no causal attribution. prj_study_im3_building_01132541700: Four bounded syntheses are retained after direct-record search: one deterministic conversion of Meta's rounded 2024 Henrico water-withdrawal observation and three governed, descriptive county comparison gaps. No construction, operating, supplier, household, tax-receipt, incentive-cost, or public-service-cost model is added because the public record lacks the needed project-specific bases and arbitrary allocation shares would create false precision. Every retained estimate is visibly modeled, unallocated to the selected building, non-additive, and noncausal. prj_study_im3_campus_00019988712: Residual synthesis after the Meta Prineville direct-evidence audit. One medium-confidence unit conversion carries Meta's rounded 2024 facility-level water-withdrawal observation from megaliters to gallons because the shared direct register has no compatible annual-withdrawal metric. The three low-confidence county benchmark comparisons were removed: even with fit-sensitivity envelopes and explicit non-causal labels, they do not materially improve decisions about this campus and remain vulnerable to concurrent Meta expansions, Apple's separate campus and unrelated county changes. No supplier, construction, payroll, household-spending, tax-abatement, public-service-cost or fiscal-net model is retained because local inputs and same-scope evidence are insufficient. prj_study_im3_campus_00231769626: Residual synthesis after the Google The Dalles public-source audit. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparison gaps are retained because the direct record does not identify causal county outcomes. Each benchmark uses the available 2001-2005 pre-opening history, excludes all study counties from a 20-county inverse-distance-weighted donor pool, and carries a fit-sensitivity envelope. No model converts broad investment or permit values to jobs, onsite contractor counts to supplier output, utility-system loads to campus consumption, tax bills to payments, or unmatched incentive formulas and public costs to a fiscal net. prj_study_im3_campus_00675108684: Dedicated last-resort Boydton model-eligibility pass under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. Retained syntheses are limited to exact arithmetic over cited compatible observations: a five-fiscal-year average of the operator-reported portfolio property-tax total, its explicitly conditional same-scope public-cost break-even identity, and annual sums of identified LVL/Herbert Fund 301 components. All remain unallocated, modeled rather than observed, and non-additive to their source totals. COF phase investment, operating headcount, construction, resources, suppliers, induced effects, causal comparisons and net fiscal impact were rejected because overlap, timing, scope or required project inputs remain unresolved.

project_description: Microsoft San Antonio is Microsoft's data-center property at 5150 Rogers Road in Bexar County, Texas, developed under the 2007 Westover Hills agreement and documented as operating by November 4, 2013. The exact-site boundary includes a 36.235-acre appraisal parcel with 463,350 square feet of commercial improvements plus separately assessed Microsoft personal property. This account does not allocate broader Bexar-and-Medina activity, later San Antonio campuses, or unlocated company totals to the site.
